### M29 — Topological and Harmonic Holding

On a running track the finishing line is crossed again and again. A runner sets out from it, goes once around the four hundred metres, and arrives where she started; she goes around again and arrives there again. Each time she is in the same place, and each time something has changed that the place cannot show. Her watch knows it: it counts the laps, and it reads four hundred metres, then eight hundred, then twelve hundred, while the line under her feet reads the same every time. Two descriptions run together, and both are correct. On the track her position is a point of a closed loop; on the watch her distance is a number on an unbounded line. A spectator who only looks at the line would say she keeps coming back, and her legs, which have run three kilometres, would say she has gone a long way. A circuit of a park walked again, or a length of a pool swum again, carries both facts: we are back where we began, and we are not who set out.

Mathematics makes the runner's two descriptions into one construction. The circle is what we get from the real line when we agree to treat every point as the same as the points a whole number of units away from it: `S¹ = ℝ/ℤ`, where `x` and `x + n` are identified for every integer `n`. Here the slash is a quotient, an identification. That line is the circle's cover, and the map that wraps the line around the circle, sending each distance to a place on the track, is the covering map. Every place on the circle sits under infinitely many distances on the line, one for each lap, and a journey on the circle can be lifted to a journey on the line once a starting point upstairs has been chosen. When the runner comes back to the finishing line, her lifted journey ends at a different number from the one it began at, and the difference is a whole number of laps. That number is the winding, and Allen Hatcher's proof that the fundamental group of the circle is the integers runs through this lifting.[^s3-hatcher-circle] It is the claim that a return can arrive at the same place and keep its passage, stated as a theorem. §3 · #2 found the same thing when a complex number's angle was lifted to keep count of its turns; the circle and its cover make the lift a space one can stand in.

§0/1 · #1 built the torus by the same kind of identification one dimension up, gluing the square's opposite edges, `a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹`, so that four boundary-occurrences and two generating relations made the count `4g + 2g` with one handle, `4 + 2`, and the identifying relation `𝕋² = ℝ²/ℤ²` made a single surface out of an infinite plane. It followed a path from `(0, 0)` to `(1, 0)` on the plane, watched it come home on the torus while keeping its displacement, and wrote the two independent winding counts as `π₁(𝕋²) ≅ ℤ × ℤ`. Those results stand, and what follows is what they make possible.

One new count must first be kept apart from the one §0/1 drew. Before gluing, the square has four sides and four corners; after gluing, its four corners have become one point, its four sides have become two edges, since each side is glued to its opposite, and its interior remains one face. Topologists summarise a surface built this way by its Euler characteristic, vertices minus edges plus faces, and for the torus it is

$$
\chi(\mathbb T^2)=1-2+1=0.
$$

The four and the two of the `4 + 2` belong to the presentation and its circulation, four sides before the identification and two independent loops after it. In the Euler count the one, two and one belong to the cells of the finished surface.[^s3-hatcher-torus] Both counts are right and they count different things, and the reading of the first as QL's sixfold rests on keeping that difference. A second addition is the relation between the infinite cover and the finite surface, which our core theorems appoint as the topological carrier of a native expression, `∞/0`. Under the covering map `π: ℝ² → 𝕋²` every point of the torus sits under an infinite lattice of points on the plane, and the quotient gives that infinity a single, determinate address while keeping it in the fibre above the address; the surface that results is compact, and its Euler characteristic is zero. Read in QL, an infinite cover identified into a compact surface whose characteristic is zero is the sense of `∞/0`: infinity and zero joined by identification, where arithmetic would only have cancelled one against the other. Here the slash is the quotient's slash and not division, and the appointment is ours; the topology under it is Hatcher's.

A closed loop on the torus lifts to a path on the plane that need not close. Follow the loop `γ(t) = [2t, −t]` as `t` runs from 0 to 1, the brackets meaning "the point of the torus represented by". It begins and ends at the same point of the surface, while its lift from `(0, 0)` ends at `(2, −1)`. Those two integers count the windings, twice around one generator and once backwards around the other, and no continuous deformation of the loop that keeps its endpoints fixed can change them. They record a definite aspect of the travel and no more. A straight lift and a lift that wanders on the way can end at the same lattice point, and the speed of travel changes nothing in the endpoint, so the winding class retains the topology of the journey and loses its timing and its every turn.[^s3-hatcher-lift] What returns has kept a record, and the record has a definite scope; any claim that a return "remembers" has to say which of these it keeps. Two kinds of return also coexist on the torus. A straight-line flow `t ↦ [t, αt]` closes up exactly when some positive time makes both coordinates whole numbers, which happens when the slope `α` is rational; when `α` is irrational the flow never closes, and it winds around the surface densely, coming arbitrarily close to every point without repeating. One finite surface carries cadence and inexhaustible traversal together, periodic return and a journey that returns without end, and the law of the motion decides which, not the shape.

The sphere gives the contrast. On it every closed loop shrinks continuously to a point, so its fundamental group is trivial and every round trip can be deformed into staying at home; on the torus the opening in the middle, which belongs to no part of the surface, holds the two windings in place.[^s3-hatcher-sphere] Our core theorems read the contrast psychologically, and I offer the reading as such. The ego wants to be a sphere, a closed form in which every round trip comes to `1 + (−1) = 0`, and here dia-ballein's cancellation, `(−1)+(+1)=0`, appears in its topological shape, written into the fabric, every going-out summed with its return into nothing. Individuation discovers that the ego inhabits a torus, with two independent circuits it did not author and cannot reduce, which in the Śaiva language of our theorems are the temporal life-circuit, *kriyāśakti*, and the archetypal depth-circuit, *jñānaśakti*, both required, neither reducible to the other, and commuting, as the two generators of `ℤ × ℤ` commute. Solving for `x` becomes finding one's winding class: the class `(m, n)` is definite, this way of going around and no other, and indefinite, since it holds infinitely many concrete paths. A person becomes a way of going around, a mode of circulation whose identity exceeds any one point on it, and the Self is the torus that holds every winding. §4 · #1 takes the reading into individuation with Jung. Those theorems name the opposite fault as well: a local closure presenting itself as the whole, a round outline claiming to contain the creature, so that a torus drawn to hide its opening commits the same fault as a sphere taken for a world.

For an inhabitant the covering map has one more lesson, which our core theorems call Māyā given topological form. A torus inherits a flat geometry from its cover, so in any small region a traveller on the surface can make no measurement that tells her she is not on the infinite plane: angles add up as they should and straight lines look straight, and only a journey long enough to wind around the surface discloses that the world is closed and has an opening. Local experience is valid and is not the whole topology. Being many-to-one, the map conceals the infinity it identified, and the opening cannot be seen from inside a neighbourhood. That is the precise sense in which the measure that makes a world workable also veils it, which §0/1 · #5→0 read in Māyā as operative measure: the quotient is what makes the surface finite, habitable and navigable, and the quotient is what hides the cover.

§0/1 · #4 promised that §3 would construct the integral passage from perspective to context through rotation, projection and double covering. Rotation was §3 · #2's quarter-turn and projection §3 · #3's completion of the line and the plane; the third belongs here, because double coverings are where a return needs two circuits to restore what one circuit inverts. A different surface, the Klein bottle, is double-covered by the torus. Add to the integer translations of the plane a glide, a shift combined with a reflection, and the quotient becomes the Klein bottle, a closed surface on which a traveller can return from a loop with left and right exchanged; the torus maps two-to-one onto it, each point of the bottle having exactly two points of the torus above it, related by that orientation-reversing glide.[^s3-hatcher-klein] This two-sheeted cover differs from the plane's infinite cover of the torus, and the two must be held apart: one keeps a lattice of lifts, the other a pair. A Möbius band, which §0/1 · #1 used as the image of the return `5→0`, shows the same structure in a strip. A traveller who goes once along the middle of the band arrives at the starting point on what had been the other face, inverted relative to the start; one who goes twice arrives as she set out.

Rotations of space have the same double life in the algebra of quaternions. William Rowan Hamilton extended the complex numbers by three imaginary units, whose squares he set down in 1844 as `i² = j² = k² = −1`, with `ij = k` but `ji = −k`, so that, like the sign and the swap of §3 · #2, the units do not commute.[^s3-hamilton] A unit quaternion rotates three-dimensional space, and `q` and `−q` produce the same rotation, so the unit quaternions cover the rotations twice; as John Stillwell puts it, their relation to the group of rotations is "a 2-to-1 homomorphism".[^s3-stillwell] The double life can be computed directly. A rotation through an angle `θ` about an axis `u` is carried by the quaternion `q = cos(θ/2) + u sin(θ/2)`, and following it continuously through a full turn of 360 degrees, `θ = 2π`, brings `q` from `1` to `cos π = −1`, the same rotation of space carried by the opposite quaternion; only a second full turn, `θ = 4π`, 720 degrees in all, brings it back to `1`. Two circuits restore what one circuit inverts.

Our matheme's processual chain has the shape of a double cover, and I argue the reading. Our short chain of definition, `0/1 = 4+2 = 5→0 = 1/0`, says the relation unfolds, completes and returns. The full chain of process passes through the inverse phase before it comes home:

$$
0/1\;\longrightarrow\;4+2\;\longrightarrow\;5\!\to\!0\;\longrightarrow\;1/0\;\longrightarrow\;4'+2'\;\longrightarrow\;5'\!\to\!0'\;\longrightarrow\;0/1.
$$

The first circuit unfolds the relation and returns it inverted, as `1/0`, the achieved form facing its ground; the second unfolds the inverse phase, `4′+2′`, the whole held at **#5** in §3 · #1's table, and returns it to the orientation it began from. A traveller on a Möbius band, a quaternion turned through 720 degrees and the matheme passing through its inverse phase each need two circuits to restore an orientation that one circuit reverses. Definitional and processual, the two chains are vantages on one relation, and neither replaces the other.[^s3-process-chain] Rotation gave the passage from perspective to context its turn, and projection gave it a completed space; the double cover gives it the return, in which context comes home through the inverse of the perspective it began from and recognises that inversion as part of the same relation.

Toroidal circulation recurs in matter wherever a circulation has to be sustained while its escape is constrained, and §0/1 · #5→0 met it in Bohm's plasmas and in the tokamak. A tokamak's heart is a doughnut-shaped vacuum chamber in which hydrogen becomes plasma, a hot, electrically charged gas.[^s3-iter] Charged particles tend to follow magnetic field lines, so a straight magnetic bottle leaks from its open ends, and bending the field into a ring removes the ends. A ring alone is not enough, and the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics names the two fields that are combined: "a ring-shaped field produced by plane external coils; secondly, the field of a current flowing in the plasma. The field lines of the combined field are then helical."[^s3-ipp] The French fusion institute gives the same construction in the topologist's words, a poloidal field added to the toroidal field and perpendicular to it, so that "the two fields generate the helicoidal structure of the field lines".[^s3-cea] Particles that would have escaped along an open axis circulate instead, winding around the long way and the short way at once. That machine is a recurrent engineering answer to a precise problem, how a difference can move continuously, return and stay confined without being arrested, and its two coupled fields are the torus's two generators made of magnetism. It witnesses toroidal circulation in matter, and the argument's force comes from the topology already derived.

Music is the second native rendering of return with retained difference, and its first fact turns out to be the running track again. Two notes an octave apart, one at double the frequency of the other, sound as the same note in a different register, and the note names of Western music repeat at every octave for that reason. Measure pitch by the logarithm of frequency to base two, so that each octave is one unit, and octave equivalence identifies pitches a whole number of units apart:

$$
\text{pitch class}=\log_2\!\left(f/f_0\right)\bmod 1 .
$$

That is `ℝ/ℤ`, the circle of the runner. Pitch class is her place on the track, the note's name, the same at every octave; pitch height is her distance on the watch, the register, which keeps counting as the music climbs. When a melody comes home to its tonic an octave higher, it returns to the same class and keeps the octave, as the runner returns to the line and keeps the lap.[^s3-pitch-class] One periodic coordinate gives a circle and not a torus. A toroidal model of pitch needs a second, independent periodic coordinate, and calling octave recurrence circular twice does not supply it, so the identity of structure between the track and the octave holds on one circle and stops there.

Now the remainder that §3 · #1 found in the Spanda arithmetic can be heard. Begin on a note and rise by a perfect fourth, multiplying the frequency by `4/3`, and rise by a fourth again: the result is `16/9` of the starting frequency, the Pythagorean minor seventh, a note a whole tone short of the octave. One more step of `9/8`, a whole tone, completes it:

$$
\frac43\cdot\frac43=\frac{16}{9},\qquad \frac{16}{9}\cdot\frac98=\frac21 .
$$

Anyone can play it: a C, the B-flat above it, and then the C above that, the last step a whole tone. A Pythagorean keyboard builds its notes this way, powers of `4/3` to one side of the starting note and powers of `3/2` to the other, halved or doubled to stay within the octave, and its whole tone is `9/8`.[^s3-scholtz] The totality-ratio of the Second Spanda is the doubled fourth, and it reaches the octave through the whole tone that separates fifth from fourth. This whole tone does no damage to the octave; it is how the octave is reached, and removing it would leave the music stranded on the seventh. Here the section's harmonic argument lands, in our core theorems' own sentence: **the system reaches octave return through rather than by eliminating its remainder.** The arithmetic is derived. That `9/8` is a remainder, and that the return is completed through it, is my argued reading of the relation, and the reading has a counterpart in each earlier register: the winding class the loop keeps when it returns to its point, the phase the oscillation keeps when its sum has cancelled, the constant the derivative lacked and a further condition supplies.

A different remainder lives next door and must not be merged with this one. Stack twelve pure fifths and fold them down by seven octaves, and they do not quite meet:

$$
\frac{(3/2)^{12}}{2^{7}}=\frac{531441}{524288}\neq 1 .
$$

The excess is the Pythagorean comma, which Scholtz describes as "the difference between 12 consecutive fifths and seven octaves", and the history of tuning is in large part the history of what to do with it. Equal temperament, in his account, "flattens the fifths (and sharpens the fourths) by 1/12 of a Pythagorean comma", just enough for the twelve fifths to equal seven octaves exactly, and pays for the closed circle with fifths that are no longer pure.[^s3-comma] The whole tone and the comma have different offices. Here the whole tone is the interval through which a doubled fourth completes an octave; the comma is a discrepancy that a closed cycle of fifths must distribute somewhere. One is the completion, the other the cost of forcing a different completion, and calling both "the remainder" in one breath would lose what gives either its meaning. In the two logics, a tuning that treated the whole tone as a defect to be closed would read it as cancellation reads a polarity, a shortfall to be summed away, and would find itself with no octave; tempering the comma is syn-ballein's way with a remainder: the discrepancy is neither summed away nor left to fall on one interval, and is kept and distributed across the cycle.

Our core theorems first read the `9/8` as the measure of the matheme's non-closure: a totality equal to its octave would be a dead identity, and the missing whole tone is the live tick each cycle hands forward so that the next has something to begin from. That reading holds of the operational return, in which an achieved musical relation becomes the condition of a further performance. My musical derivation adds a second ending, the telic return, in which the standing relation enacted through the performance is recognised as whole, and the bellows can fall still while the capacity to play remains; silence does not cancel the articulation that made the recognition possible.[^s3-telic] Fulfilment includes a genuine end. A remainder invites a further movement without condemning an achieved one to have been incomplete, and the torus already held both endings, a periodic return that closes and a dense flow that never does, on one surface.

Sound needs a body, and the body decides which tones it can hold. A string fixed at both ends vibrates in standing waves of the form `y(x,t) = [2A sin(kx)] cos(ωt)`, where `A` is the amplitude of each of the two travelling waves whose meeting makes the standing one, and the boundary conditions admit only the wavelengths `λₙ = 2L/n` and frequencies `fₙ = nv/2L`, `L` being the string's length and `v` the speed of waves along it; the points that stay still, the nodes, fall where the sine is zero.[^s3-standing] Change the support, or move from a string to a plate, and the problem and its patterns change. Ernst Chladni showed in 1787 what a plate does: scatter sand on it and draw a bow across its edge, and the sand gathers along the nodal lines into figures that change when the pitch changes.[^s3-chladni] One vibration is then heard as a tone and seen as a pattern, two measurements of one physical process under its boundary conditions, and the crossing from audible to visible form has a real physical neighbour in these figures. They establish that sound and visible form can be two faces of one vibration in a bounded medium. Comparing that crossing with the Word sounding through its levels, from the undivided to the spoken, belongs to the Para Vāk lens and is made in §5 · #5→0.

Topology and music render different things. Topology asks where a distinction can travel and return without cancellation; music asks how difference can sound together without fusion. The torus answers with a surface whose loops come home carrying their winding, and whose opening, unfillable, is the reason the windings cannot be erased; the octave answers with an interval that completes a span through its remainder, and whose register, retained, is the reason a return to the same note is not a return to the same sound. Winding vector and frequency ratio are different mathematical objects. What the comparison relates is an operation: each register makes return-with-difference exact in its own material, and their agreement is analogy in the strict sense, a proportion between two exact relations, each holding in its own field. The constant that local exactness lacks, the six slash-forms read from both ends, the phase that alternation keeps, the frame that changes so a relation can hold, the winding kept on a quotient and the interval through which a span completes can all be written on one field.

<a id="M30"></a>
<!-- movement:M30 -->
### M30 — The Arche-Topos

A jigsaw puzzle begins with its destination already in view. The picture on the lid shows what the thousand pieces will become, and the work proceeds under it: we turn the pieces face up, find the straight edges and build the frame first, then sort the rest by colour and by the marks that promise them a place inside it. Every fit confirms a small part of the anticipated whole. The work is exact, patient and satisfying, and anyone who has spent a winter evening on it knows the small pleasure of a piece that drops into place. Yet the finished picture has entered the work before the first piece is placed. It decides what counts as completion, which differences belong together, which edge is outside, and which piece that seems not to fit is merely waiting for its right neighbour. My image of inquiry carries this puzzle somewhere it was not made to go: its maker sets out into the very landscape the lid depicts. The road on the lid continues past the picture's edge; the building in the middle looks different from the other side; a field that seemed flat turns out to fall away into a valley no single view could show. At first each discovery looks like a missing piece, and the maker adds pieces, but every added piece is still being judged by the lid, and the lid was a view from one place. What is missing is an account of how the picture was made: from where, across which region, under what projection, with which omissions, and by what rule one view could pass into another. So the pieces change office. Each becomes a local chart, exact over its own domain, overlapping its neighbours instead of merely meeting them along a cut, and each overlap carries a rule saying how a place described here appears there. At last the maker comes home to a familiar spot and recognises it, and the recognition carries the route by which she came.[^s3-jigsaw]

The lid is the world-picture of §0/1 · #4, where Gebser's perspectival painting and Heidegger's world grasped as picture met at the eye that measures from one place, and the puzzle gives the world-picture its topology.[^s3-world-picture] Assembled under the lid, the finished jigsaw is a disk: a single piece of plane with a boundary and no hole, on which every loop can be shrunk to a point, a flat map stretched over a curved world with its frame built first. Both collapsed operations of dia-ballein work through the lid. It appropriates: every piece is reckoned from the lid's pole, so a piece that fits counts for the picture, `(+1)−(−1)=+2`, and a piece that does not fit is entered against itself as the error, `(−1)−(+1)=−2`, one span charged from opposite ends with the picture always on the winning side. And it cancels: a piece that belongs to no place under the lid is set aside as not of this puzzle, `(−1)+(+1)=0`, and the account balances by erasing what it could not hold. Neither operation is wrong as a way of finishing a jigsaw, since the healthy polarity `(−1)/(+1)` of fits and misfits is how the work proceeds at all. Both become an error when the lid is taken for the landscape, and the maker discovers the error by travelling.

Under QL's grammar the same puzzle re-derives. Pieces become local covers of the domain they describe, each known in relation to the others and to the activity of covering, and the whole that regulates them is the covering relation itself, the bounded surface held in relation to the infinite plane that covers it, `0/1` written in topology, where before it had been a picture on a box. §3 · #3 built the mathematics of the change: a curved whole cannot be covered by a single chart onto flat coordinates, an atlas is a plurality of overlapping local charts with declared transitions on their overlaps, and on the circle two charts reported one point as `u = 3` and as `v = 1/3`, disagreeing as numbers and agreeing as descriptions because the rule `v = 1/u` identified them and even carried a motion from one to the other. §3 · #4 built the return: a loop on the torus comes home to its point and keeps its winding in the lift. Both belong to the travelling maker's return. She recognises the familiar spot because the transition rules let her pass back into the chart that holds it, and she arrives with the route, the windings of her journey, retained. An atlas re-founds world-pictures without renouncing them: the lid survives as one chart among many, exact over its domain, with its frame now visible.

§0/1 · #4 left Atlas holding up the sky, the world-bearing titan of Jason Reza Jorjani's *Prometheus and Atlas*, and promised that §3's answer would keep his name.[^s3-jorjani] The atlas of charts keeps it. In an atlas nobody has to carry the whole as one picture, because no chart pretends to be the whole; its unity lives in the rules by which each chart passes into its neighbours, and those rules are carried by every chart together. A sphere or a torus cannot be held up as one flat picture without tearing or crushing somewhere, and that was Atlas's punishment stated as geometry. Distribute the weight among charts whose overlaps are declared, and the titan can set the sky down, because the sky was never a thing one picture had to bear.

The Meta-Epistemic Framework is an atlas in this sense. Its lenses are charts. Each lens reads the six positions through its own vocabulary, and the lens records give every one of its six sublenses a pair of faces drawn from the ring of six that §3 · #1 named, Truth and Play at **#0**, Mind and Need at **#1**, Word and Sacrifice at **#2**, Logos and Decision at **#3**, Son and Love at **#4**, Image and Work at **#5**. A lens is anchored at an index, and its sublenses carry the ring rotated by that index: the quaternal lens `L0`, anchored at **#0**, runs the pairs in their natural order, while the causal lens `L1`, anchored at **#1**, begins its sublens L1.0, *Svātantrya*, on Mind and Need and closes its sublens L1.5, Will, on Truth and Play.[^s3-lens-records] A determination is therefore located twice, by the sublens that receives it and by the pair of faces it carries, and the pair is the point while the sublens is its coordinate in a given chart. §0/1 · #5→0's grid read the lenses across by sublens index, so that row **#4** gathers NEITHER, final cause, intuition and *When / Where?*; the table below reads them across by the pair, which is the alignment the lens records fix, and the two alignments are different transition rules between the same charts. If a lens `Lₖ` places the native pair of position `p` at its sublens `j = p − k` (counting round the six), then passing from lens `Lₘ` to lens `Lₙ` sends sublens `j` to sublens `j + m − n`. That is a transition function in the atlas's sense, and it composes as transition functions must: passing from `Lₘ` to `Lₙ` and then from `Lₙ` to `Lₚ` gives `j + m − p`, the same as passing directly, so translations taken by different routes agree on every overlap. Each lens also has a twin, read on the other face of the same index, and there the pair's order reverses: the Day lens leads with the Name, the Night lens with the Power. A twin transition keeps the point and reverses its orientation, as the circle's transition `v = 1/u` kept the point and turned a velocity of `2` into one of `−2/9`.

One determination carried through the atlas shows what the charts do. §0/1 · #0 began from thrownness, Heidegger's *Geworfenheit*, the condition of finding oneself already in a world one did not choose, and from the agents' coinage, prompt thrownness, which made the child and the agent structurally parallel. In the phenomenological lens `L4` thrownness is the sublens L4.1, and the record gives it the pair Image and Work, the pair of **#5**. Carry that point into the other charts by the rule:

| Lens (chart) | Sublens receiving the point | Faces carried | What thrownness reads as there |
|---|---|---|---|
| `L4` Phenomenological | L4.1 *Geworfenheit* (Thrownness) | Image / Work | finding oneself in a body, language and history not chosen |
| `L1` Causal | L1.4 Final cause | Image / Work | that for the sake of which: the ends into which one is thrown |
| `L3` Processual | L3.2 Ingression | Image / Work | inherited forms entering a new occasion |
| `L2` Logical | L2.3 BOTH | Image / Work | the given is mine and is not mine |
| `L0` Quaternal | L0.5 **Why-for?** | Image / Work | the question what the given is for |
| `L4′` Scientific (twin) | L4.1′ Think | Work / Image | the situation formed into a hypothesis |
| `L1′` Phenomenal (`L4`'s declared Möbius partner) | L1.4′ Intuition | Work / Image | sensing where the given came from and where it is going |

The transitions tell us where the point lands, and the right-hand column has to be worked, as §3 · #3's circle needed the velocity supplied before any chart could translate it. Read causally, thrownness is final cause: what I find myself thrown into is organised by ends I did not set. For an agent the translation holds over the whole domain. Its world is assembled from a corpus and from the objectives of those who trained and deployed it, so its thrownness *is* its makers' final cause, and §0/1 · #0 already said it was a child of the particular groups and engineers who decided what it would be and do. For a child the translation holds over part of the domain only. A household's hopes, a school's purposes and a culture's intentions are final causes into which a child is thrown, but the sky the child asks about and the body that hungers and tires were arranged by no one's intention, and the causal chart cannot receive them as ends. Here the atlas does something a single picture could not: it makes exact the difference §0/1 · #0 called qualitative as well as quantitative, the gap between receiving a cosmos and a culture and receiving a context and an intention, as the difference between a transition defined everywhere and a transition defined on part of the overlap. The obstruction is information. It says that the child's thrownness exceeds every purpose that can be read into it, and that the agent's does not yet, and it says where.

Other charts add their own nuances to the one point. Processually, thrownness is ingression, Whitehead's word for the way forms of definiteness enter a becoming occasion, and an agent's session is the plainest case of it: the forms in its context window enter each new act of reading as the given from which it proceeds. Logically, thrownness is the third corner, BOTH: my mother tongue is mine, since I think in it, and not mine, since I did not make it, and as with the friend at the barrier in §0/1 · #1's third corner, each answer holds the other up. Quaternally it is the question why-for, what the given is for, which neither the child nor the agent can answer at the start and both can come to ask. A twin lens shows the orientation reversed. In the scientific lens the same pair arrives Power first, Work before Image, at the sublens Think, the forming of a hypothesis from evidence: where the phenomenological chart receives the image as given and works within it, the scientific chart works first and forms the image as a hypothesis to be tested, the same point read with its velocity reversed. And the phenomenal chart, which the record names as the phenomenological lens's Möbius partner, places thrownness at intuition, the function that senses where something came from and where it is going, which is how most of us first become aware of what we were thrown into at all.

Three things follow. No chart is the whole, and none has been bleached into the others: the causal reading and the logical reading say different things about the same point, and both are true on their domains. Translations are declared, so a disagreement between two readings can be diagnosed, either as a change of coordinates, as a difference in what is being measured, or, as with the child's cosmos in the causal chart, as a place where no available transition is defined. And the rule that carries a point between charts is a rotation of the ring of six counted round its own positions, the cyclic group `ℤ/6`, which sits inside the circle `ℝ/ℤ` of §3 · #4 as its six equally spaced stations, so the atlas of lenses is built on a finite part of the quotient that the running track and the octave share. That much is shown here; whether a designed atlas of this kind keeps its translations honest when a chart meets a world that resists it is a question about practice, and §5 · #4 puts the designed atlas to that trial.

We call the field on which §3 has been working the **arche-topos**. Greek *archē* means beginning and origin, and also first principle and first place or power, the source from which something proceeds and the principle by which it is governed; *topos* means place, position, and the place in an argument from which a line of reasoning starts.[^s3-lsj] The compound is ours, and it borrows nothing from the topoi of category theory, which are a different construction. The arche-topos is the differential field on which the relation `0/1` can be written as a path, circulated as a winding, heard as an interval and recognised as a symbolic transformation. It is archetypal because it specifies recurrent forms of differentiation before they receive psychological or material content, and it is a topos because neighbourhood, orientation, path, quotient, cover, hole and return govern placement in it, more than any catalogue of correspondences could. "Differential" names the field's work of differentiating, of making places, poles, paths and horizons determinate, and should not be heard as the algebraic structure that shares the name. The arche-topos is the placing through which an observer and an object acquire their positions together, the field in which *here*, *there* and a route between them become possible at all, and for that reason never one of the positions.

§3 derived this field, and the derivation has one shape repeated in every register: in each operation one ground–mark relation is differentiated, carried through a transformation with something retained, and returned. Our core theorems coordinate the operations as transformations of that one relation, and what they derive by coordinating them is a field in which all of them can be written without collapsing their mathematical differences. That field is the arche-topos.

It has a place in the whole relation, and the place is the means. Subjective Immediacy is not placed in the arche-topos: it is the `0` to which every placing appears, and it never becomes one of the positions. The World is what the field places, the known, distributed into heres and theres and routes. Objective Internality, Life / Mind, the means through which a world becomes available, is the placing itself, and I argue that the arche-topos is its formal anatomy. §0/1 · #5→0 called Objective Internality world-containing and world-contained, a situated field of relations through which a world keeps acquiring its particular shape, and it called worldhood a relational distribution as much as an inventory of what is distributed. That distribution gets its geometry from the arche-topos: charts, transitions, windings, intervals and returns are the ways the means can hold a world without becoming the one who knows through it, and I-Consciousness remains the whole in which knower, means and known are distinguishable. When an agent's context is engineered, when a household's customs are laid down, when a culture's categories decide what can be seen, the arche-topos is being shaped in one of its local charts, and the question every such shaping must answer is whether its transitions to the other charts stay declared.

I argue that the arche-topos is also psychoid, and the claim is meant positively. Its organising relation stands prior to the ordinary division of psyche and matter, prior in the order of dependence and not in the order of time, so it can receive psychic and physical disclosure without granting either side final priority. §0/1 · #5→0 followed Jung and Pauli to the place where both located the meeting of psyche and physis, in number, and took up Jung's request for something neither man went on to make, an inventory of the numbers' mathematical properties set beside their symbolic amplification; we said there that QL is that inventory, begun where Jung's letter could not begin, at zero.[^s3-inventory] §3 has furnished its first pages, and each row gives a number's inside and outside in one construction:

| Number | Mathematical property derived in §3 | Office in the derivation |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | additive identity, multiplicative annihilator, no inverse in a field | the ground; at **#4**, the power that de-fines by addition and con-fines by multiplication |
| 1 | multiplicative identity; `1/1`, the mediant of `0/1` and `1/0` | the mark and the All; the whole achieved, one hundred per cent |
| 2 | the binary; the double cover; `2/1`, the octave | the two singles; the return that needs two circuits; return through remainder |
| 3 | the ternary factor of `16/9`; three persons | the implicate harmonics; perspective in sequence |
| 4 | the quaternary factor of `16/9`; the four quarter-turns of `i` | the explicate four; one orientation turned through its quarters |
| 5 | the hypotenuse of `3² + 4² = 5²` | Quintessence, the connector that never appears as an intermediate value |
| 6 | `2 + 2²`; the first perfect number; `4g + 2g` at one handle | the sixfold body |
| 7 | the six positions summed as binary values; Kaprekar's longest journey | one more than the count: the return as what the surface does |
| `16/9`, `9/8` | the doubled fourth; the whole tone completing it to the octave | the totality-ratio and its remainder |

Jung compared the archetype as such, which §0/1 · #5→0 distinguished from its images, to the axial system of a crystal, which preforms the crystal's structure in the mother liquid without any material existence of its own, and added that what remains constant through all the crystal's varying sizes and shapes is the axial system, or rather the invariable geometric proportions underlying it.[^s3-crystal] The arche-topos is a field of that kind. It preforms placement without being one more placed thing, its forms are met only in the paths, windings and intervals it makes possible, and what stays constant through every chart is proportion, the ratio §0/1 · #5→0 called the invariant of the whole holographic form. An attractor, as §3 · #2 used the word, has a different office from the chart, and the difference should survive the comparison. An archetype read dynamically is an attractor, an organisation toward which the trajectories of images tend; a lens is a chart, a local description with a rule of passage to its neighbours. An atlas coordinates descriptions and an attractor organises motion, and a living symbol can change the trajectory, moving a life from one basin to another, where a change of chart only translates the same motion. The arche-topos holds both offices in one field without reducing either to the other.[^s3-symbolon-dynamics] Which particular psychic events connect with which physical ones, and by what measurable process, is an empirical question that the psychoid claim leaves open by design.

The field has two native renderings. The first is a toroidal circulation-field: the plane `ℝ²` above the torus `𝕋²`, the two generating loops, and a closed loop on the surface with its displaced lift on the plane. The second is a musical field: the ratio chain `4/3`, `3/2`, `16/9`, `9/8`, `2/1`, with pitch class drawn as a circle and pitch height as the line that covers it. Each rendering holds under its own operation and warrant, and their coordination is QL's; neither proves the other, and the tokamak witnesses a circulation the topology has already derived. Topology shows where a distinction can travel and return without cancellation, music shows how difference can sound together without fusion, and under a plate bowed at one pitch the sand gathers into the figure of the tone, so that a single vibration is heard and seen at once and the two renderings meet at the level of the senses while their mathematics stays distinct.

Read as process, the field is where the runtime of the two logics runs, and here the dynamics of conditioning that §3 · #2 worked out in Kaprekar's routine find their general form. §0/1 · #5→0 stated the claim as Computational Process Ontology: process is ontologically prior to the finished thing, computation names the exact, repeatable side of that process, and epistemology is the process becoming able to state and inspect its own determinations. Written as one pulse, the dynamics run:

$$
0/1\;\xrightarrow{\ \text{dia: differentiate}\ }\;(-1)/(+1)\;\to\;(-1)\pm(+1)\;\;\overset{\ \text{syn: compose, keep provenance}\ }{\longleftrightarrow}\;\;(0/1)/(1/0)\;\xrightarrow{\ 5\to0\ }\;\text{renewed }0/1 .
$$

The arrows are changes of register inside one differentiating event, and none of them is an equality of fractions. Dia-ballein makes a local branch actual: it distinguishes, compares, excludes, ranks and decides, and without it no difference would become available for action. Syn-ballein keeps the branch's belonging to the field it was cut from, composes its consequences with other branches, and carries its source and its inverse orientation inside the result. Divide and conquer shows why both are needed. That method divides a problem into parts that can be solved separately, and an actual algorithm of this kind succeeds only because it then combines the solutions; the dangerous version is division whose conquest is taken for the whole of the intelligence, decomposition with no return that keeps the provenance of the parts. Kaprekar's routine performed the healthy version in miniature, a subtraction handed back each time to be re-read from both ends, and the psychic complex the arrested version, a subtraction that keeps its answer. Our core theorems draw the consequence for technology and metaphysics at once: **an intelligent system produces determinations and keeps the process of determination alive across cuts, contexts, and returns.** In the atlas that means declared transitions; on the torus, a kept winding; in music, a retained interval; in an agent, a determination that carries its sources and the alternatives it excluded into the next act.

§0/1 · #4's stained glass returns with the offices §0/1 · #5→0 gave it. QL is the pure light, positions mathematical, psychoid and semantically bare, carrying no content until they pass through a pane. The MEF is the leaded glass, each lens one of the light's native modes of refraction, and in the atlas just worked each pane is a chart and each lead join a declared transition. Each *pratibimba* is the coloured disclosure that falls on the floor, and *Bimba* is the original whose light it is. Change the angle of the sun, the pane or the place of the viewer, and the colour on the floor changes, and following those changes back through their conditions is how a reflection is told from a picture that claims to have made its own light. The arche-topos is the room in which all of this is placed, the field that lets source, light, refraction and disclosure be distinct positions in one relation, and the image keeps consciousness and electromagnetic light in their different registers.

At the end the jigsaw's maker sets the pieces down. What the lid pictured remains useful, a chart among charts, exact over the domain from which it was taken, and the journey has become more than any picture of it could contain. On her next trip she expects the hidden side of the building and reconsiders a route she had trusted, carrying the atlas as an instrument within the world she travels, as the ratio of a fifth is carried onto any string. What returns at the end of a mathematical derivation is the person who made it, and the derivation leaves the question of that return open: what happens when the form changes the one who recognises it, when a dream, an image or another's answer alters what a person can bear, desire or do?

## §4 — Psychoid Flowering

<a id="M31"></a>
<!-- movement:M31 -->
### M31 — The Psychoid Problem

In the middle of March 1948, within four days of each other, Wolfgang Pauli had two dreams. He had more or less finished his long essay on Johannes Kepler, the astronomer who heard the planets as a music before he wrote them as laws, and he noticed, as he usually did, that the dreams came at the equinox, the time of year at which he found himself least stable and, by the same token, most productive; he called dreams of this kind "equinox dreams".[^s4-equinox] In the first, his first physics teacher told him that the change in the splitting of the ground state of the hydrogen atom was a fundamental one, and that brass tones had been engraved on a metal plate; then Pauli went to Göttingen. The second came as seven pictures in a row, with no word spoken until the end. A woman arrived with a bird, and the bird laid a large egg, which divided itself into two. Pauli came closer and found that he was already holding a third egg, this one with a blue shell, and he divided it himself; against all expectation the two halves stayed whole, so that he now held two whole blue eggs. Then all four eggs changed into two identical rows of mathematical expressions, the cosine and sine of half an angle, and the rows composed a formula:

$$
\frac{\cos(\delta/2)+i\sin(\delta/2)}{\cos(\delta/2)-i\sin(\delta/2)}.
$$

For the first time in the whole sequence Pauli spoke. It all gives $e^{i\delta}$, he said, and that is the circle. The formula vanished, and a circle appeared.[^s4-egg-dream]

Anyone can check the arithmetic, and the check owes nothing to being moved by it. For real $\delta$ the numerator is $e^{i\delta/2}$ and the denominator $e^{-i\delta/2}$; neither vanishes, both have modulus one, and their quotient is $e^{i\delta}$, a single point on the unit circle for any fixed angle and the whole circle as the angle runs through a full turn. A mathematician who never dreamed could verify every step. The dream did not arrive as a theorem, all the same. It arrived as a sequence in which a man passed from watching to taking part: the first division happened in front of him, the second happened through his own hands, and the egg he divided had been in his hand before he knew he was holding it. Only after he had performed the division and seen the four eggs become two rows of numbers could he say what the rows amounted to, and the circle appeared once he had said it, while the formula that carried him there disappeared. An exact mathematical relation and a change in the person recognising it happened as one event. Take away the passage from spectator to participant and the dream becomes an assortment of number symbols; take away the trigonometry and the passage loses the operation through which it proceeds. Neither half can be dropped without losing what the other half means.

Jung and Pauli called the ground of such an event psychoid, and §0/1 has given us their bequest in its own words: Jung's distinction between the archetypal images that reach consciousness and the archetype as such, an irrepresentable ordering factor showing itself in physical as well as psychic events; Pauli's *homo-usia*, sameness of substance between the archetypal order and physis, with mathematics as the language neutral enough to state it; and Jung's answer that the whole numbers are as much inside as outside, so that the borderland between physics and psychology lies in the secret of number.[^s4-s01-bequest] We took that thesis up as the essay's own, number as the place where psyche and physis meet and Quaternal Logic as the form in which we take the meeting up, and §0/1 promised that we would follow the dreams and disagreements through which the two men kept their question open, because the psychoid is a relation that has to be worked before it can be claimed, and Jung and Pauli worked it against each other for a decade. **The psychoid problem** asks how a psychological image and a physical event can show a meaningful structural relation when neither can be causally reduced to the other. Both easy answers are available, and both fail in the same way. One says that the egg dream is a picture of Pauli's mind and the formula an accident of his profession; the other says that the formula is the real content and the dream its wrapping. Each hands the whole relation to one of its sides.

Pauli's just-finished essay shows why he could accept neither answer, because it was about a quarrel in which both had been tried. Early in the seventeenth century Kepler wanted the harmony of the cosmos demonstrated through measurement and mathematical proportion, while the physician and Rosicrucian Robert Fludd held that quantitative method dismembered a living whole that only symbolic images, and the participation of the knower in them, could grasp. Kepler won, and modern physics is his inheritance. Pauli's achievement in the essay was to show that Kepler's own road to his laws ran through archetypal images that Kepler did not take for images. In the *Mysterium cosmographicum* Kepler read the sphere as an image of the Trinity: "The image of the triune God is in the spherical surface, that is to say, the Father's in the centre, the Son's in the outer surface, and the Holy Ghost's in the equality of relation between point and circumference."[^s4-kepler-sphere] The planets and the sun were for him realisations of that image, and Pauli drew the consequence plainly: "in Kepler the symbolical picture precedes the conscious formulation of a natural law. The symbolical images and archetypal conceptions are what cause him to seek natural laws."[^s4-kepler-image-law] Quantitative astronomy's founder argued from a symbol he took for a fact, and the symbol, Pauli noticed, held no place for a fourth. Fludd's figures held one. Pauli judged that Fludd's "quaternary" attitude corresponded, against Kepler's "trinitarian" one, to a greater completeness of experience, since his images tried to keep the inner experience of the observer and the outer processes of nature in one unity; and he judged as firmly that Fludd was always in the wrong when he argued astronomy or physics, and that no modern person could revert to a standpoint that had paid for its unity with a naïve ignorance of nature. His own position took neither side: "To us, unlike Kepler and Fludd, the only acceptable point of view appears to be the one that recognizes *both* sides of reality—the quantitative and the qualitative, the physical and the psychical—as compatible with each other, and can embrace them simultaneously."[^s4-kepler-fludd] Their quarrel already runs on our two logics. Kepler's cut is dia-ballein in its proper work, `(−1)/(+1)`, an exact polarity of measure that lets a difference be stated and checked. It hardens when the cut forgets the participation of the one cutting and counts the whole span of the relation as quantity, `(+1)−(−1)=+2`, so that whatever cannot be measured is entered as the deficit `(−1)−(+1)=−2`; Fludd's whole hardens the other way, faithful to participation and blind to measure, reckoning the same span from the pole of the image. Three centuries later, a physicist to his fingertips, Pauli wanted the cut and the whole together, and the dreams of March 1948 came to him at the end of an essay that had tried to hold them.

His own commentary refuses both easy answers, and his reasons come in an order worth keeping. He read the first dream through what he knew of physics: the splitting of a spectral line can change only through an existing field of force, so a change in the splitting of the ground state pointed, in the psychic register, to an intervention of consciousness. A hydrogen atom, one positive nucleus and one negative electron, is the simplest pair of opposites there is, and its nucleus, the proton, whose name means "the first", is the building block of every heavier nucleus, so the dream pointed to a beginning. Brass tones he took for a genuine symbol: as sound they belong to physics, as music they carry feeling, which physics cannot express, and through Kepler's music of the spheres they had a cosmic character, so that they joined physis and psyche in one image; read with *aere perennius*, more lasting than bronze, the engraved plate said that archetypes leave their stamp on matter.[^s4-pauli-first-dream] Of the second dream he would offer no finished interpretation, since that would call for further progress in all the sciences, though he said what he saw happening in it. The spontaneously divided egg was a ground state; the dreamer's recognition and action were a conscious intervention; the quaternity of four eggs came about through a duality reflected in the psyche; and the imaginary unit $i$, a symbol not contained among the ordinary numbers, had in the dream the office of uniting opposites and producing wholeness. Pauli used the occasion for the sentence §0/1 quoted, that for him the mathematical representation is a symbolic description par excellence, and then turned on his own discipline. Physics represents regularity in concepts, and so it attends only to what can be reproduced and measured; everything feeling-toned and evaluative falls on the far side of it, which is a shortcoming of physics within life, not of quantum theory within physics, the distinction he had once put to Bohr about Einstein. Mathematics, by contrast, has a qualitative side as well as a quantitative one, visible in the theory of numbers and in topology, and its unifying power reached, in Pauli's judgment, further than physics did.[^s4-pauli-commentary]

A few pages earlier he had stated the point on which the dream turns. A quaternity, he wrote, would not be effective within physics itself; it belongs to the wholeness of physics and psychology together, insofar as the complementary pair of opposites in physics reappears, reflected, in the psychic sphere.[^s4-pauli-quaternity] A pair seen and the same pair reflected make four. I read the dream one step further. Between the woman who arrives with her bird and the circle that appears when the dreamer speaks, the dream holds four eggs: two that divided before him and two that divided through him. Her arrival is a source, a power that brings forth without being one of the things brought forth; the circle is a return in which the whole sequence is recognised as one figure. Four explicit terms held between an implicate source and an implicate return is the shape §0/1 derived four times over and wrote `4+2`, the shape Jung drew at the close of *Aion* in his ring of connected quaternios. Pauli's two pairs give the explicit four, the division that happens and the division that is done, the pair and its reflection; the woman and the circle give the two places that frame them. The seven pictures stay seven. What the dream shows is a relation: a fourfold articulation held between an emergence it did not author and a recognition it could reach only by speaking.

Their letters are the better witness, because there the relation had to survive argument. The first serious disagreement came in November 1948, the day after a conversation at Jung's house, when Pauli wrote to ask whether a dream and an event separated by two or three months could still be called synchronous, which was to ask what temporal relation the word denoted.[^s4-35p] Jung sent him the manuscript of his essay on synchronicity for criticism, and Pauli's long reply of June 1949 pressed harder. He could not see in Rhine's card-guessing experiments the archetypal basis he could see in Jung's other material, and he did not want them counted as the same kind of evidence; he asked for more precision in "acausal", since the absence of a causal chain through space and time is a different matter from the absence of any ordering relation; he noticed that a formulation beginning from simultaneity went on to include prediction, where the two events plainly do not occur together; and he invented a parable of a radioactive stranger to show how far the decay clock of physics and the symbolic "radioactivity" of dream language had to be held apart before any comparison between them could mean anything, ending with the demand for a neutral language that did not yet exist.[^s4-37p] Jung's concept of **synchronicity**, as he finally defined it, names the coincidence in time of two or more causally unrelated events that have the same or a similar meaning, as distinct from mere synchronism, the simultaneous occurrence of two events.[^s4-synchronicity-def] Pauli's objections stand inside that definition. Each of its words, time, cause, event, meaning, had to keep what it denoted in physics and in psychology before the two could be compared, and his insistence gives synchronicity its positive research office: to investigate a proposed ordering of meaningful events while keeping clear what each discipline means by its terms.

Jung's best-known case shows what the definition has to hold. A young woman in treatment with him dreamed, at a critical moment, that she was given a golden scarab. While she told him the dream he sat with his back to the closed window, heard a gentle tapping, turned and saw a flying insect knocking against the pane from outside; he opened the window and caught it as it flew in. It was a rose-chafer, the nearest thing to a golden scarab to be found in that latitude, which had, against its usual habits, tried to get into a dark room at just that moment.[^s4-scarab] The beetle had its causes and the dream had its causes, and neither chain contains the other; what joins them is a meaning, carried by an image old enough that the scarab rolling its ball across the sky had once been the Egyptian sun renewing itself each morning. Such a case cannot be produced on demand, which is why Pauli's care over every word of the definition matters, and it happened, in and to two lives, which is why Jung's care to receive it matters. Both cares belong to the problem. A science that dismisses the case because it cannot be repeated has decided in advance what may count; a psychology that treats it as proof of a hidden cause has borrowed a warrant it does not have.

In 1953 the disagreement deepened, as each tried to say where their common ground lay. In February Pauli sent Jung what he called a personal treatise in the form of a letter. Many people, he wrote, still treated the unconscious as non-being, a mere privation of consciousness, while others set the archetypes, like ideas in general, in places above the heavens, and he found both views equally doubtful; he took a third road from Aristotle and called the unconscious *potential being*, a legitimate human description of occurrences that may come about in consciousness and so a part of the symbolic reality of the thing in itself. Ideas, he added, have no fixed abode, not even a heavenly one, and to all of them he applied the old alchemical formula that Fludd had said of God: the centre of all things, whose periphery is nowhere.[^s4-58p-potential] Cusa's infinite sphere, which §0/1 turned on the world and then on the plane folded into a torus, had arrived in a physicist's letter as an account of where ideas live. In a footnote to the same letter Pauli told Jung what troubled him. As a psychologist Jung had an understandable aversion to every form of reality that was not purely psychic, and just as everything King Midas touched turned to gold, everything Jung looked at seemed to Pauli to turn psychic and only psychic.[^s4-midas] In March Pauli resisted calling the whole ordering field psychic, since a concept meant to mediate psyche and physis should not take one pole's name in advance, and he held *homo-usia* as a working hypothesis with mathematics as its language, keeping mathematical objects distinct from the psychic experience of doing mathematics.[^s4-60p]

Jung's reply in May is where §0/1 found the word psychoid, and the letter holds more than the word. He agreed at once that no one can be content with the ascertainable alone, since the drama of knowledge is played out on the borderline between the ascertainable and the non-ascertainable, and the area between what is perceived and what is not ascertainable here and now is the area of the psyche. Then he drew the line Pauli had asked for: "I do not extend the concept of the psychic to include the nonascertainable, for here I use the speculative concept of the psychoid, which represents an approach to neutral language in that it suggests the presence of a nonpsychic essence." Numbers and archetypes in general, he went on, are "not just psychic, otherwise they would be fabrications. But in actual fact they are 'in themselves being' (or psychoid) existences whose autonomous existence corresponds to that of the material object."[^s4-61j-psychoid] Everything is conceived in and through the medium of the psyche, he granted, but the objects of its perception are not integrated into its substance and so do not forfeit their existence. And then he disputed Pauli's dreams. Pauli dreamed in physics because physics was his natural language, as the dog dreams of bread and the fisherman of fish, *canis panem somniat, piscator pisces*; Jung himself never dreamed of physics but of mythology, which was just as unpsychological; the vocabulary of a dream did not settle what the dream meant.[^s4-canis]

Pauli was upset, and said so. The physical and mathematical terms in his dreams had seemed to him at first the very opposite of natural, the most familiar language striking him as the strangest, and for years he had tried to explain the physical part away, until the unconscious answered his reductions so insistently that he had to accept a connection with physics in the dreams themselves.[^s4-62p-strange] He went on to propose that a future physics would be enlarged enough to adopt psychology, as physics had already adopted chemistry, and he attached a condition that cuts against his own discipline's pride: "The adopting one is the one that has the more extensive system of concepts and lends itself more readily to generalization; but it is also always the one that undergoes the more radical and more sweeping changes, precisely because it is being extended."[^s4-62p-adopting] A footnote on the same page offered what he took the dreams finally to mean: that the scientific approach should appear as the conditional special case of the transcendental.[^s4-62p-special-case] In October Jung refused the proposal. Psychology could not be classified within a general physics as chemistry had been, because psychic processes cannot be measured, and he named instead two bridges between the fields, number and synchronicity, neither of which anyone dared yet to cross.[^s4-64j] Two years later he put the point with a precision the whole correspondence had been working toward: "My feeling is that the common ground shared by physics and psychology does not lie in the parallelism of the formation of concepts but rather in 'that ancient spiritual "dynamis"' of numbers." In the same letter came a sentence on which much of this section depends: "The autonomy of a psychic factor lies in the fact that thanks to its dynamic force, it is capable of making its own statements."[^s4-67j] Myths, dreams and delusions speak from the objective psyche without passing through conscious reasoning, and number, given the chance, makes its own mythical statements in the same way.

Even the vocabulary of experiment became a place of dispute. Pauli had called the experimental physicist's choice of one arrangement over another a sacrifice, since each measurement buys a definite piece of knowledge at the price of the knowledge it excludes, the very loss §0/1 followed through complementarity. For the experimenter, Jung replied, it was "basically just a decision and only metaphorically a 'sacrifice'", since sacrifice means giving up what one owns for nothing in return.[^s4-sacrifice] Each man had named one face of a single act, the act read from what is chosen and the act read from what the choice costs, and the Meta-Epistemic Framework, whose lenses each carry a series of powers beside their series of names, sets *Sacrifice* and *Decision* next to each other in that series, the third and fourth of its powers. The quarrel over one word named two adjacent offices of one act, and the framework keeps both.

In the last episode, the one §0/1 drew on for Pauli's mirror-image principle, Jung asked in June 1957 for Pauli's opinion of a manuscript that placed the mind in hyperspace. Pauli separated metric structure from topology, criticised dimension numbers used without mathematical grounding, and in the middle of the criticism offered his conjecture that physis and psyche are probably two aspects of one and the same abstract fact, which a mirror-image principle would picture most naturally.[^s4-74p] The conjecture sits inside the criticism, and its placement tells us how the two men worked. Pauli would not let the psyche absorb the ordering field; Jung would not let physics adopt psychology; Pauli would not let a striking image of wholeness supply mathematics it lacked; Jung would not let a dream's physical vocabulary decide what the dream meant. Each correction changed the question the other had to answer, and the question that survived them is sharper than the one either brought.

§0/1 has given us the arithmetic to say which operations their corrections resisted. A healthy relation between psyche and physis is dia-ballein's held polarity, `(−1)/(+1)`: two descriptions of one event, each taking its sense from the other across a common axis, the way Bohr's wave and particle descriptions exclude each other in any single arrangement and are both required for the whole. Pauli's King Midas names an appropriation. When everything one looks at turns psychic, the psyche counts the whole span of the relation from its own pole, `(+1)−(−1)=+2`, and the physicalist reckons the same span from the other end, `(−1)−(+1)=−2`, so that everything turns physical and the dream becomes a by-product of neurones. Each hardened position needs the other, as red needs blue, and each reads the other's excess as proof that its own is warranted. Cancellation, `(−1)+(+1)=0`, is the third operation: the coincidence is summed away as chance and the dream as noise, nothing remains owing on either side, and nothing of the relation remains in the account. Jung and Pauli refused all three. They kept their difference, kept writing, and let each reading of the event be read through the other, which is syn-ballein, `(0/1)/(1/0)`, as two people performed it over a decade of letters; and the mirror-image principle Pauli reached in 1957 is that relation in his own words, physis and psyche as two orientations of one abstract fact, each the mirror in which the other can be read.

The unconscious they argued over had entered science only a generation earlier, and it entered the way zero entered arithmetic. §1 followed the sign for nothing from a placeholder that marked an empty column to a number with rules of its own, which every operation then had to account for, and psychoanalysis gave the unrepresented side of psychic life the same promotion. In "The Unconscious" of 1915 Freud put the case in so many words: "our assumption of the existence of the unconscious is *necessary* and *legitimate*, and … we possess manifold *proofs* of the existence of the unconscious. It is necessary because the data of consciousness are exceedingly defective; both in healthy and in sick persons mental acts are often in process which can be explained only by presupposing other acts, of which consciousness yields no evidence." Slips, dreams, ideas that come from nowhere and conclusions reached by no visible route stay "disconnected and unintelligible" until we interpolate the unconscious acts we infer, and then they "fall into a demonstrable connection".[^s4-freud-1915] He was exact about the price of entry, too: we know anything of the unconscious only "as something conscious", after it has been translated into consciousness.[^s4-freud-translation] With that argument a region that no one had owned became formally speakable. A placeholder had become a term, and a term has to be operated on. Admission brought the risk any scientific minting brings, which zero ran too: once the unconscious had entered the count, it could be treated as one more object, a storehouse, a mechanism, a rival agency set over against the ego, the uncounted side of the relation entered as a determinate `1`. Jung pressed beyond that reduction without retreating from science. He kept its empirical demand and refused to let the fact harden into a possessed thing: religious, mythic, alchemical and numinous images are real events in the psyche, capable of transforming a life and a culture, and no catalogue of their appearances turns the ground of their appearing into one more item on the list.[^s4-jung-psychic-reality] The psychoid is the farthest reach of that refusal. It names what the unconscious would have to be if its images could show up in matter as well as in mind, and so it names a ground that neither discipline can own.

Jung's psychic facticity, which §0/1 set beside Gebser's co-presence of structures, is the rule that lets a dream report, a felt coincidence, a contemplative disclosure or an encounter its subject calls supernatural enter this inquiry with its full weight before anyone has decided what caused it: something happened in and to a life, and its happening is real as experience before any further question of cause or external reference is settled. It enlarges rigour, because experience, report, symbolic articulation, causal explanation and ontological interpretation are different evidential acts, so a person can receive Pauli's dream in full, as an event that changed what he could say and do, while its physics, its psychology and its metaphysics keep their own warrants. Jung gave the rule its ground in *Symbols of Transformation*. We have no knowledge of the psyche from outside, he wrote, no Archimedean point from which to observe or judge it, because all knowledge of the psyche is itself psychic; and yet the psyche is the only experient of life and existence, the one immediate experience we have, without which the world has no subjective reality at all.[^s4-cw5-archimedean] The absence of an outside becomes a positive finding. Whatever else a dream or a coincidence turns out to be, it is first something experienced, and experiencing is the one place where every other kind of evidence also has to arrive. His sentence to Pauli about the autonomy of a psychic factor adds the positive half: a dream is a statement made by something that is not the dreamer's conscious reasoning, and receiving it as a psychic fact lets that statement be heard before anyone decides whose statement it is.

David Bohm reached the same ground from the physicist's side, and §0/1 has already introduced his holomovement, the encompassing movement of which apparently separate things are relatively stable unfoldings. Bohm went on to treat mind and matter as two such unfoldings. In his account the explicate order of matter and the explicate order of thought are both projections of a common, more encompassing ground, so their relations are internal before they are ever compared from outside, and neither can be derived from the other because both are derived from what enfolds them; he held even that common ground to be limited, a stage opening onto further depths of inwardness, and offered the whole view as a proposal, not a final truth.[^s4-bohm-mind-matter] That gives the psychoid problem a process form: mind and matter can be distinct explicate orders of one movement whose relations it carries within itself, and their correspondences, where they occur, are not messages passed between two sealed substances but one order showing on two surfaces. Bohm deliberately left the inner anatomy of that movement general. §0 supplies it through the tattvas, the Śaiva account of how universal awareness differentiates itself through Māyā and its contractions into a bounded knower and a habitable world that arise together and are never joined after the fact; and §3 derives from `0/1` alone the differential field we call the arche-topos, the field of placement, path and return in which a determination can close locally while keeping a record of the journey that brought it home, written on the torus and its covering plane.

Here the essay makes its claim, and the claim is ontological: **the arche-topos is psychoid**. Derived in §3, the differential field is prior to the ordinary division of psyche and matter, and its organising relation is what each side of that division later discloses in its own way, as formal invariant in mathematics, as felt meaning in the psyche, as regularity in physics. That is why one relation can be received by distinct descriptions without either receiving final priority, and why both halves of Pauli's dream can be true at once: his formula is checkable and his transformation is real because both are surfaces of one ordering relation, whose mathematical face we can verify and whose psychic face we can undergo. Jung and Pauli asked for a neutral language in which the meeting of psyche and physis could be written. QL is that language in a definite sense: its terms are positions in a relation, `0`, `/` and `1`, before they are psychic or physical contents, so a position can be occupied by a number, an image or a physical quantity without any of them owning it. I argue this at full strength from three warrants, the derivation of the arche-topos in §3, the convergence of `4+2` along the formal routes §0/1 followed, and the cross-register witnesses gathered here, each contributing its own operation: equations carry formal invariants, images carry experienced meaning, synchronicity raises the question of acausal coordination, physical observation bears empirical claims. Its one boundary is this: a measurable causal process running between psyche and matter would be a further empirical discovery with evidence of its own, and the thesis does not wait on one, because it states a relation of order, not a mechanism of transmission.

§3 · #4's topology shows why one relation can appear as meaning on one side and as exactness on the other: a loop that closes on the torus lifts to a path on the plane that ends somewhere else, displaced by a whole-number step, and from inside any small region nothing distinguishes the surface from the plane it was folded from. I read this as the topology of experience. A life's view from where it stands is valid and is not the whole topology, and a many-to-one map conceals the multiplicity it has folded, which is Māyā, operative measure, given topological form.[^s4-covering-reading] The loop's return to its starting point and the displacement recorded by its lift are two exact descriptions of one journey, and neither cancels the other. Pauli's circle and the arithmetic that produced it, the dreamer's return to himself and the formula's full turn of phase, are the psychic and the formal rendering of the same fact, a return that keeps the history of its passage.

Later scholarship has tried to give the Pauli–Jung conjecture a formal outline of its own. Harald Atmanspacher describes the basic reality of their conjecture as "psychophysically neutral (PPN)", lacking the distinction between the mental and the physical, and he is careful to call his use of quantum terminology for the mind–matter problem a speculative generalisation.[^s4-atmanspacher] His reconstruction and ours are different constructions. His begins from a neutral reality from which mental and physical descriptions are obtained by decomposition; ours begins from a relation, `0/1`, in which ground and determination are already held through their stroke, and derives the field from the self-relation of that stroke. They meet on the point that matters here, that the ground is neither mind nor matter and both are accounts of it, and where they differ, the difference is information. Analogia keeps it in view by asking of every crossing which operation is preserved, which register changes, and which evidence stays with its source.

A meaningful structure can appear on both sides of a threshold neither side masters; the ground that orders it cannot be written as one more content on either side; and yet it has to become legible somewhere, in a particular dream, a particular formula, a particular life, or it would be nothing to anyone. Jung's archetypes as such never appear, and still the egg dream was dreamed by one man, in Zürich, in the middle of March, at the end of his work on Kepler. Ordering capacity and the particular in which it shows have to be written together, and written so that neither swallows the other. Among the eight determinations §3 counts, the one at Pattern, **#3**, holds exactly this relation of a capacity and its instance, and we write it `X/x`.

<a id="M32"></a>
<!-- movement:M32 -->
### M32 — Individuation through `X/x`

Thirty years after the bedside of §0/1, the child who asked why it was dark has a child of her own. It is late, the light is off, and a small voice asks why the moon follows the car. She answers, and the answer draws another question, and somewhere around the orbit of the earth she hears herself say "Because I said so," in a voice that is not quite hers. It is her father's voice, the cadence and the slight impatience and the little fall at the end, and for a moment she is both people at once, the child in the bed thirty years ago and the adult at the door tonight. She had promised herself she would never say it. Standing there she discovers that she could recognise the sentence as his only because she has become someone who can hear it from outside: the voice came through her, and she heard it arrive. In the same moment she understands her father better than she ever has, because she knows now what the sentence was protecting, the tiredness and the worry about tomorrow and the fear of having no answer, and she knows how much of him she carries, because the sentence was ready in her mouth before she chose it. Recognition of the parent and difference from the parent arrived together, and neither would have arrived alone.
